questions.q: Explain the concept of the investment multiplier.

answer.text: The investment multiplier explains how an initial increase in investment leads to a much larger increase in national income and employment. When investment rises, it creates income for some people, who then spend a part of it, creating income for others, who spend again, and so on through successive rounds.

Suppose new investment is made in building a factory. The wages and payments made become income for workers and suppliers. They spend a portion of this income on goods and services, which becomes income for shopkeepers and producers, who in turn spend part of it. This chain of spending multiplies the original investment several times over in the form of total income.

The size of the multiplier depends on the marginal propensity to consume. It is given by the formula, multiplier equals one divided by one minus the marginal propensity to consume. The greater the tendency to spend, the larger the multiplier.

answer: Thus a small rise in investment can produce a large rise in national income.

questions.q: What is aggregate demand, and how do its components determine the level of income and employment?

answer.text: is the total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given level of income, and it determines output and employment.

list: Its components are consumption, investment, government spending and net exports
The economy is in equilibrium where aggregate demand equals aggregate supply

answer.text: Output adjusts to meet planned spending.

list: If aggregate demand is too low, output and employment fall, causing unemployment
If it is too high relative to capacity, prices rise; so managing aggregate demand is central to keeping full employment without inflation

questions.q: What is meant by full employment, and what causes involuntary unemployment?

answer.text: is a situation in which everyone willing and able to work at the going wage can find a job — it does not mean literally no unemployment.

list: Some frictional unemployment always exists as people change jobs
Full employment means there is no involuntary unemployment
It occurs when people want to work at the current wage but cannot find jobs
It is caused mainly by a shortfall of aggregate demand, so that firms do not produce and hire enough — a case for government action to raise demand
